weather_report:
Late morning on Rottnest feels hushed under a quilt of uniform cloud, the light gentle and silvery, water and scrub alike losing their hard edges. Sunshine will be scarce today; the forecast keeps the sky overcast into the afternoon and toward early evening, so expect more glow than glare. UV is softened by the cloud but not erased—around midday it can still nip exposed skin—so think of shade and a dab of sunscreen even without the sparkle. The day is clear in its own way: distant shapes look honest and matte, the horizon less a line than a suggestion.

Dress for mild, changeable comfort: a breathable layer with a light jacket you can pocket if the air settles. With the sun muted, it’s a fine time for unhurried things—an easy spin along the paths without squinting, a quiet visit to the museum, or a slow coffee where the view does most of the talking. If you walk the shoreline, the flat light is kind to photographs and sketches; if you read, the pages won’t glare back. Let the afternoon unfold at a humane pace, and save the bright ambitions for another day.
